title: The waterfall, actually animated this time
question: Does this read as a waterfall now — a pool that spills over an edge, falls, and lands in another pool? And is the fall itself still too thin?
context_md:
**Please ignore the previous card (`290b82`) — I built it wrong.** Putting two files in one item makes the page treat them as a two-frame sequence, which is exactly what you saw. A GIF has to be its own item. The animation was fine all along (24 frames, looping); my card flattened it. Same content here, correctly attached.

You said it looked like it came from nowhere and went nowhere. Both halves are now built.

**Finding a source pool was impossible, so the pass cuts one** — and the measurement that killed the search is what made cutting work. Requiring the ground to *drop* behind a cliff lip matched nothing in 24 worlds, which means the opposite holds: the shelf behind a rim stands at or above the lip for a median 107–120 columns. That is exactly the back wall a pool needs. So `springs` walks that shelf, cuts a tapered bowl into it, and fills it to the brim. The pool has two ways out — the cliff right there, and the far end of the shelf a hundred columns away — and it reaches the cliff first.

Still unfinished, and I have not touched it: the fall is narrow. `render.rs` dims a liquid toward black by fill, so a thin sheet reads darker than it should. Tell me if it bothers you and I will go at it directly rather than guessing.
